facts.statement: Tornieria is a genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaur found in the Lindi Region of Tanzania.
facts.quote: Tornieria ("for Tornier") is a genus of diplodocid sauropod dinosaur from the Late Jurassic in Lindi Region of Tanzania.

facts.statement: German paleontologist Eberhard Fraas discovered two sauropod specimens at Quarry A in the Tendaguru Beds in 1907.
facts.quote: In 1907, German paleontologist Eberhard Fraas who was working the Tendaguru Beds in German East Africa (presently Tanzania), discovered two sauropod specimens at a single site ("Quarry A").

facts.statement: Eberhard Fraas originally named the species Gigantosaurus africanus and G. robustus in 1908.
facts.quote: In 1908 he named these respectively Gigantosaurus africanus ("African giant lizard") and G. robustus ("Robust giant lizard").

facts.statement: Richard Sternfeld renamed the genus Tornieria in 1911 to honor the German herpetologist Gustav Tornier.
facts.quote: Another German paleontologist, Richard Sternfeld, renamed the Tanzanian sauropod Tornieria in 1911, making the two species Tornieria africana and T. robusta.

facts.statement: Werner Janensch re-evaluated Tornieria in 1922, concluding that T. africana was actually Barosaurus africanus.
facts.quote: A re-evaluation of Tornieria in 1922 by Werner Janensch concluded that one species, T. africana, was actually an African species of the North American sauropod genus Barosaurus: Barosaurus africanus.

facts.statement: Kristian Remes concluded in 2006 that Tornieria is a distinct and valid genus separate from Barosaurus.
facts.quote: However, later researchers proposed generic distinction between the American and the African form. In the early 21st century this usage became prevalent and in 2006 Kristian Remes in a review concluded that Tornieria was indeed distinct and a valid genus.

facts.statement: According to Gregory S. Paul, Tornieria was 25 meters long and weighed 10 metric tons.
facts.quote: Tornieria was a large sauropod; according to Gregory S. Paul, it was 25 m in length, and weighed 10 metric tons.

facts.statement: A maximum known femur length of 138 centimeters suggests Tornieria reached 26 meters in length and 23 tons in weight.
facts.quote: Tornieria era un saurópodo grande, con una longitud máxima conocida de fémur de 138 centímetros, lo que sugiere un animal del mismo tamaño que Barosaurus, 26 metros y 23 toneladas.

facts.statement: Tornieria is characterized by having robust hind legs and short tibiae.
facts.quote: Se caracterizaba por poseer patas traseras robustas y tibias cortas.

facts.statement: Remes (2006) concluded that Tornieria is a member of the subfamily Diplodocinae.
facts.quote: After performing a cladistic analysis, Remes (2006) concluded that Tornieria was the sister taxon of a clade formed by Barosaurus and Diplodocus. It would thus be a member of the Diplodocinae.

facts.statement: The genus Tornieria was established by Sternfeld in 1911.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Sternfeld, 1911

facts.statement: The species T. africana was originally described by Fraas in 1908.
facts.quote: species_authority: Fraas, 1908

facts.statement: Fossils of Tornieria were discovered in the Tendaguru Formation in 1908 by the German paleontologist Eberhard Fraas.
facts.quote: Los restos de Tornieria fueron encontrados en la Formación Tendaguru, en 1908 por el paleontólogo alemán Eberhard Fraas.

facts.statement: The generic name Tornieria honors the German herpetologist Gustav Tornier.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico hace honor al herpetólogo alemán Gustav Tornier.

facts.statement: Richard Sternfeld proposed the name Tornieria in 1911 for two species, T. robusta and T. africana.
facts.quote: Sternfeld en 1911 propuso el nombre Tornieria, con dos especies T. robusta y T. africana.

facts.statement: In 1961, Werner Janensch suggested T. africana was an African variety of Barosaurus and T. robusta belonged to a macronarian later named Janenschia by Wild in 1991.
facts.quote: Una revaluación de Torneria en 1961 por Werner Janensch propuso que la especie, T. africana, fuese considerada una variedad africana de Barosaurus y la otra especie T. robusta, considerada un macronario, que fue llamado Janenschia por Wild en 1991.

facts.statement: Tornieria is currently considered a distinct genus from Barosaurus with two species, T. africana and T. gracilis.
facts.quote: Actualmente se considera que Tornieria es un género separado de Barosaurus con dos especies, T. africana y T. gracilis.

facts.statement: A 2006 cladistic analysis concluded that Tornieria is the sister taxon to a clade formed by Barosaurus and Diplodocus.
facts.quote: Después de realizar un análisis cladístico, Remes en 2006 concluyó que Tornieria era el taxón hermano de un clado formado por Barosaurus y Diplodocus.

facts.statement: Tornieria is classified as a member of the subfamily Diplodocinae.
facts.quote: Sería pues un miembro de las Diplodocinae.

facts.statement: Tornieria lived during the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, from 152.21 to 143.1 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Tithonian (152.21 to 143.1 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are 7 recorded fossil occurrences of Tornieria in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 7

facts.statement: A 2026 study found evidence of at least five independent origins or reversals of pneumaticity in anterior caudal vertebrae among neosauropods, including Tornieria africana.
facts.quote: A study on the caudal vertebrae of Cetiosaurus sp., "Cetiosaurus" glymptonensis, Wamweracaudia keranjei, Dicraeosaurus sattleri, Tornieria africana and Giraffatitan brancai, providing evidence of at least five independent origins and/or reversals of pneumaticity of anterior caudal vertebrae in Neosauropoda, is published by Beeston et al. (2026).

rejected.statement: Tornieria differed from Barosaurus and Diplodocus by having plesiomorphic hindlimb proportions with a short lower leg.
rejected.quote: However, it differed from the American form by details in the anterior caudal vertebrae and from Barosaurus and Diplodocus both by its plesiomorphic hindlimb proportions with a short lower leg.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'plesiomorphic hindlimb proportions with a short lower leg'

rejected.statement: Tornieria fossils date from the Tithonian stage of the Late Jurassic.
rejected.quote: The remains are from the later strata of the Tendaguru, the obere Dinosauriermergel or "Upper Dinosaur Marl", dating from the Tithonian.
rejected.reason: quote not found verbatim in the source

rejected.statement: Bivens, Greenfield, and Curtice (2025) debated that T. gracilis is a validly named species with correct authorship by Chure & McIntosh (1989), contrary to Remes (2006) who suggested it was a nomen nudum.
rejected.quote: However, Bivens, Greenfield and Curtice (2025) suggested that T. gracilis is not a nomen nudum but a validly named species, since the name has been made available by Chure & McIntosh (1989) as a subspecies of T. africana (then referred to B. a. gracilis) who explicitly credited the species' authorship to Janensch (1961), which is in accordance with the International Code of Zoological Nomenclature (ICZN) article 13.1.2; they concluded that T. gracilis is an available name with the correct authorship being Chure & McIntosh (1989) in accordance with the ICZN articles 45.5.1 and 50.1, and designated a lectotype in accordance with the ICZN articles 74.1 and 74.7.
